episodes.207674: A surface trough, diurnal heating, and afternoon convection, promoted showers and thunderstorms, mainly over the northwestern quadrant of Puerto Rico on November 18th. Reports of flooded roads and a landslide were received from sectors of San Sebastian.
episodes.207710: A slow moving upper level low pressure system moved down the California coast, tapping ample moisture and spreading precipitation across the state of Arizona.  This was a relatively warm storm with high snow levels, at or above 6500-7000 feet.  Dynamic support and wind shear with this storm led to some severe thunderstorms.  Heavy rain falling over ground saturated from the previous weekend's storm led to flash flooding and elevated creek flows.
episodes.207936: Numerous afternoon showers and thunderstorms, tracking eastward across central Indiana, had updrafts intensify from an approaching upper shortwave trough.  Effective vertical wind shear around 35-40 knots combined with freezing levels down to only 10,000 feet to promote growth of small hail.  Small hailstones falling below the freezing level congealed into isolated large hail from Sullivan County to Jackson County.  Sub-severe hail (0.75 inches) was also reported in Lawrence and Monroe Counties.
episodes.208021: As a surface low pressure system moved into Missouri, a warm front lifted into northern portions of the Quad State region. Ahead of the front, a SW to NE band of showers and thunderstorms developed, pushing eastward through mid-morning. Brief heavy rain resulted in a couple inches of water ponding on one of the Lloyd Expressway exits. Precipitable water values were 1.3in and 925-850mb moisture transport was quite strong.
episodes.208022: As a surface low pressure system moved into Missouri, a warm front lifted into northern portions of the Quad State region. Ahead of the front, a SW to NE band of showers and thunderstorms developed, pushing eastward through mid-morning. Penny size hail was reported on the north side of Cape Girardeau with these storms. A lack of instability prevented greater storm potential despite the effective bulk shear of 30-40kts and precipitable water values of 1.1in.
episodes.208024: A surface low drifted southeastward from Missouri through Southern Illinois and Western Kentucky during the evening hours of the 18th. Areas to the south with some afternoon clearing allowed for instability to develop, resulting in the formation of multiple clusters of storms that tracked southeastward. The most prominent of these clusters strengthened in far Southeast Missouri, moving across the Mississippi River into far Western Kentucky, at times developing embedded supercell structure. This cluster produced hail in Scott City but peaked near and just across the Mississippi River, producing a 61mph wind gust at Dorena. Effective bulk shear peaked at around 50kts near the Missouri/Kentucky border with DCAPE of 800J/kg to go along with the MLCAPE of over 1000J/kg. Precipitable water peaked at 1.3in.
episodes.208054: Another low pressure system coming inland from the Pacific lifted unseasonably moist air, producing widespread rain and spotty flooding.
episodes.208064: ABC television in Idaho Falls forwarded a photograph of a cold air funnel about 4 miles south of Aberdeen.
episodes.208533: Between the evening of November 17th and the evening of the 20th, a slow-moving upper-level low pressure system progressed through the Desert Southwest. The combination of the strong dynamical forcing from the low and well-above normal moisture values (PWATs of 0.80+) led to multiple rounds of scattered to widespread moderate to heavy rainfall and isolated thunderstorms. Most of the rain and impacts fell/occurred on the 18th and 19th, with much of central Arizona receiving rainfall totals of 1.00-2.50 and some areas receiving 3+ inches. This rainfall led to instances of flash flooding and flows in normally dry creeks and washes. Several streamflow gauges across the Flood Control District of Maricopa County's (FCDMC) network exceeded designated alarm stages and a couple gauges in far north Phoenix reached bank full. Several swift water rescues as well as road closures were reported across in or near the washes that exceeded alarm stage/bank full. ||With just enough instability (CAPE values near 500 J/KG) and high wind shear (>50 kts), several severe thunderstorms developed, including a few supercells, in Maricopa County on both the 18th and 19th. Hail was the primary severe weather impact, given the lower freezing levels. There was one report of severe hail (1+ inch in diameter) on the 18th, in Sun City Festival, and multiple reports of quarter size to golf ball size hail on the 19th, in Ahwatukee and Tempe. There was also a lot of accumulating hail, especially on the 19th when a portion of I-10 in Tolleson was covered in several inches of hail. The accumulating hail may have been a contributing factor to a partial roof collapse at Desert Sky Mall.||In addition to the flooding and hail, there were also a few reports of funnel clouds and an EF-0 tornado briefly touched down in Forepaugh, AZ, along US-60 between Aguila and Wickenburg during the afternoon hours on the 18th. The tornado caused a small amount of damage, including flipping an RV trailer.
episodes.208889: A nearly stationary frontal boundary separating an unseasonably warm airmass with temperatures in the lower 70s south of the I-64 corridor from much cooler readings in the upper 40s to around 50 degrees across central Illinois served as the focus for scattered severe thunderstorms during the afternoon of November 18th.  The storms were primarily focused south of I-72 and east of US-51 and produced hail ranging from the size of peas (0.25 inches in diameter) to as large as tennis balls (2.5 inches in diameter).

events.narrative: Wintersburg Road between Indian School Road and Osborn Road in Tonopah closed due to approximately 3-4 feet of water over the roadway from excessive runoff along Fourmile Wash. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries reported.
Penny size hail was measured as a storm tracked eastward through Cape Girardeau county, with the report submitted via mPING.

A couple inches of water covered part of the eastbound Green River Road exit of the Lloyd Expressway. Portions of the right lanes on the expressway also had puddles form. Rainfall rates peaked at around half an inch in twenty minutes, but the heavy rainfall duration was brief.
Highway 127 was flooded in at least two places, and streets around Death Valley Junction were flooded.

Old US 80 closed between Agua Caliente Rd and Desert Rose Rd due to flooding. Timing based on travel time from upstream streamflow gauge on Centennial Wash at the UPR railroad crossing. No damages or injuries reported.

Emergency managers reported flooding on PR-446 at km 0.3 intersection with PR-111 in Barrio Robles, near the Walgreens. Both lanes were inundated, and officials were planning to close the roadway. Radar estimates indicate that approximately 2 to 3.5 inches of rain had fallen in the area by the time of the report.

Emergency managers reported that floodwaters are affecting PR-109 at km 1.9 near Urb. Estancias in Barrio Culebrinas, San Sebastian. The road was partially inundated, though vehicles are still able to pass. Radar estimates indicated that approximately 2 to 3 inches of rain had fallen in the area by the time of the report.
A photo indicated the hailstones were spiky and oblong-shaped.
Goffs Road was closed due to flooding.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Stream Gauge along Jackrabbit Wash near Vulture Mine Road measured water levels rising above the alarm stage level of 2.9 feet, with flows peaking at 4.45 feet (2681cfs). Water flow this high made Vulture Mine Road as well Wickenburg Road, located approximately 5.1 miles downstream of the gauge, impassable with several feet of water likely overtopping the road. Timing was estimated based on radar and the nearby stream gauge. No damages or injuries reported.

A water rescue was reported near 377th Ave and Orange Dr in Tonopah. Two people were found stuck in their truck with water halfway up the windows before being safely rescued. Timing estimated from radar.

Emergency services reported via social media that the Rio Culebrinas overflowed its banks near Flamboyan Avenue in Urbanizacion El Culebrinas. The road was completely impassable in both directions (lanes) at the entrance of the Urbanization, near Villa Sofia.
Constellation Rd at El Recreo Drive in Wickenburg was closed due to flooding. No damages or injuries reported.

Vulture Mine Rd low water crossing at Sols Wash in Wickenburg was closed due to flooding along with a water rescue reported. A Maricopa County Flood Control District Stream Gauge at Sols Wash, just upstream of North Vulture Mine Road, measured water levels exceeding both the alarm (1.83 feet) and bank full (4.10 feet) levels, with the flow peaking at 4.17 feet (4970 cfs). Timing was estimated based on radar and the nearby stream gauge. No injuries reported.
ABC television in Idaho Falls forwarded a photograph of a cold air funnel about 4 miles south of Aberdeen.
Photographs of hail in Brownstown area as large as one to two inches in diameter.
Patton Rd between 195th Ave and 203rd Ave closed due to flooding. No damages or injuries reported.
Report of a water rescue near at Happy Valley Rd and 187th Ave. Water reportedly up to the level of car headlights. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries reported.
Needles Highway was closed at Not'Cho Road due to flooding.

Law enforcement reported a car with 2 men trapped in floodwaters in Big Bug Creek at Cordes Lakes.  One man was rescued while the other was swept away.  The vehicle was later found lodged against a tree about 2 miles from the point of entry into the water. The second occupant was found deceased two days later at the confluence of Big Bug Creek with the Agua Fria River, about 6 miles from where he and his vehicle were last seen.
Highway 95 was completely washed out at mile marker 60.4.
A USGS stream gauge on the Agua Fria River (AFHA3) near Dewey-Humboldt measured a 3 foot rise. Peak flow was measured at 458 cfs.
Report of hail up to 1 inch in diameter in Sun City Festival. Hail also accumulated to cover the ground. No damages or injuries reported.
Yavapai County Sheriff reported flash flooding with a swift water rescue along Castle Creek near Castle Hot Springs.
Media received several reports of quarter size hail measured in Scott City.

Public sent a video of a brief tornado near the intersection of HWY 60 and N 439th Avenue in Forepaugh, AZ. This tornado crossed HWY 60 and produced EF-0 damage at a property on the north side of the highway. Damage included a flipped RV trailer, minor damage to other vehicles, and loss of a garage roof. Wind speeds with this tornado were estimated between 80-85 mph. Timing estimated by radar. No injuries reported.
Emergency managers reported a landslide along Carr. 438 in Bo. Magos, near the Martir's Sport Bar area.
